title: Night of the Living Dead
tagline: Board up the windows. Stock up the snacks.

    StartersBarbara's cemetery sandwichesEgg and cress, and ham and mustard on buttered white bread, crusts off, wrapped in baking paper like a 1968 picnic.How to make it2 eggs20g mayonnaise10g cress, chopped8 slices of white bread25g butter, softened80g leg ham10g Dijon mustardBoil the eggs, cool, peel and mash with the mayonnaise.Stir in the cress.Butter the bread.Make two egg-and-cress sandwiches and two ham and mustard sandwiches.Trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into four small pieces.Wrap in baking paper for a 1968-style picnic.Black and white popcornButtered popcorn, half salted and half with pepper and black sesame.How to make it60g popcorn kernels1 tbsp neutral oil30g butter, melted1/4 tsp fine salt1/4 tsp cracked black pepper10g black sesame seedsPop the kernels in the oil in a covered pot over medium heat, shaking regularly, then divide in half.Toss one half with half the butter and the salt.Toss the other half with the remaining butter, pepper and black sesame seeds.Arrange side by side in a shared bowl.Farmhouse sardine and cheddar crackersWhatever's in the cupboard while the boards go upHow to make itAs written, serves 4Saltine crackers piled with tinned sardines mashed with lemon and parsley, sharp cheddar, and a quick pickled red onion, laid out on a chopping board.Thinly slice 1 red onion and soak it in 80ml white vinegar with 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes.Drain 2 x 110g tins sardines and mash lightly with the juice of half a lemon, chopped parsley and pepper.Slice 150g sharp cheddar.Top 24 saltine crackers with sardine, a slice of cheddar and a few pickled onion rings and lay them out on a chopping board.Fried bologna on white breadThey're coming to get you, Barbra. Eat first.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsCellar or upstairs farmhouse stewBeef chuck browned, onion, carrot and potato, stock and thyme, braised covered at 160C for 2.5 hours.How to make it800g beef chuck, cut into chunks1/2 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper1 tbsp neutral oil1 brown onion, chopped2 carrots, chopped500g potatoes, in chunks500ml beef stock4 thyme sprigs200g crusty Italian breadCut the beef and season it.Brown in batches in the oil in a heavy casserole.Add the onion, carrots, potatoes, stock and thyme.Cover and braise at 160°C, stirring once, until the beef is tender.Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the stock.Ben's beef and bean chilli with cornbreadBen pulls up at the farmhouse in a truckHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef mince chilli simmered with cumin, chilli and kidney beans, ladled into bowls over sour cream and cheddar, with hot buttered cornbread on the side.Brown 700g beef mince in batches.Cook 1 diced onion and 3 garlic cloves 5 minutes, add 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp smoked paprika, then 2 x 400g tins tomatoes and 400g drained kidney beans.Simmer 45 minutes.Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 300ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter, pour into a hot buttered pan and bake at 220°C for 20 minutes.Serve with sour cream and cheddar.SweetsPantry peach cobbler with creamTinned peach halves baked under a golden cinnamon biscuit topping until bubbling, served warm with a jug of cold pouring cream.How to make it1.7kg tinned peach halves (2 tins)1 tbsp cornflour80g cold butter200g self-raising flour60g caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon120ml milk1 tbsp raw sugar300ml pouring creamDrain the peaches, keeping a little syrup, and toss with the syrup and cornflour in a baking dish.Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and cinnamon, then mix in the milk to a soft dough.Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and sprinkle with raw sugar.Bake at 190°C until golden.Serve warm with cream.DrinksLong night spiked percolator coffeeStrong stovetop coffee sweetened with brown sugar and a nip of Irish whiskey, topped with lightly whipped cream so it floats.How to make it800ml whiskey in each glass, add hot coffee and stir.Whip the cream until just pourable and float over the back of a spoon.
